**Indikator 9c** is a clinical quality indicator used in the Danish Acute Surgery Database (AKDB) to measure 30-day mortality following acute surgery among high-risk patients. Specifically, it tracks outcomes for patients with a [[charlson-comorbiditets-indeks|Charlson Comorbiditets indeks]] score of 3 or higher, indicating a significant burden of comorbidities [^src1]. It serves as a supplementary indicator to Indikator 9b, which measures the same 30-day mortality metric but for patients with a lower comorbidity burden (Charlson Score 1–2) [^src1]. 

The data for Indikator 9c is part of the annual reporting framework managed by the Danish Clinical Quality Development Programme (RKKP) and the Danish Healthcare Quality Institute. The most recent indicator period analyzed in the 2024 report spans from September 1, 2023, to August 31, 2024 [^src1]. 

During this one-year period, mortality outcomes varied across different Danish regions and hospitals. For instance, in the Central Denmark Region ([[midtjylland-region-i-alt|Midtjylland Region i alt]]), 40 patients died within 30 days out of 152 included patients with a Charlson Score ≥ 3 [^src1]. In the North Denmark Region ([[nordjylland-region-i-alt|Nordjylland Region i alt]]), there were 13 deaths among 48 included patients [^src1]. At the hospital level, [[aarhus-universitetshospital|Aarhus Universitetshospital]] recorded 10 deaths out of 37 patients [^src1], while [[aalborg-universitetshospital|Aalborg Universitetshospital]] reported 8 deaths out of 32 patients [^src1]. Other facilities such as [[odense-universitetshospital-svendborg|Odense Universitetshospital - Svendborg]] (15 deaths out of 70 patients) [^src1], [[regionshospitalet-goedstrup|Regionshospitalet Gødstrup]] (11 out of 37) [^src1], and [[esbjerg-sygehus-grindsted-sygehus|Esbjerg Sygehus Grindsted Sygehus]] (9 out of 45) [^src1] also contributed to the dataset. Smaller cohorts were observed at hospitals like [[sygehus-lillebaelt|Sygehus Lillebælt]] (4 deaths out of 20) [^src1], [[sygehus-soenderjylland|Sygehus Sønderjylland]] (5 out of 23) [^src1], [[hospitalsenhed-midt|Hospitalsenhed Midt]] (7 out of 28) [^src1], [[regionshospitalet-horsens|Regionshospitalet Horsens]] (6 out of 25) [^src1], [[regionshospitalet-randers|Regionshospitalet Randers]] (6 out of 25) [^src1], and [[regionshospital-nordjylland|Regionshospital Nordjylland]] (5 out of 16) [^src1].

By stratifying patients based on their comorbidity index, Indikator 9c provides a crucial risk-adjusted perspective on the quality and safety of acute surgical care across Denmark's healthcare system [^src1].
